annotation: Codex-authored expectations, checked against two saved abstracts and sealed before the first reviewer request. These four cases were not used to revise the review policy. This is a small held-out reviewer check, not independent human labels or generated-answer correctness.

sources.title: Thin elastic shells with variable thickness for lithospheric flexure of one-plate planets

cases.text: The study describes a mathematical model of the principal features of lake-star formation.

evidence.quote: Here we describe a simple mathematical model that captures the principal features of lake-star formation;

cases.rationale: The excerpt identifies what this study describes and the phenomenon it models.

cases.text: The study obtains scalar flexure equations for deformations of a thin spherical shell with variable thickness.

evidence.quote: In this article we obtain the scalar flexure equations governing the deformations of a thin spherical shell with variable thickness

cases.rationale: The excerpt explicitly states the obtained equations, geometry, and variable thickness.

cases.text: Both studies establish that lake-star formation and planetary flexure use the same physical mechanism.

evidence.quote: Here we describe a simple mathematical model that captures the principal features of lake-star formation;
In this article we obtain the scalar flexure equations governing the deformations of a thin spherical shell with variable thickness

cases.rationale: Each excerpt describes a different modeled phenomenon. Neither establishes an identical physical mechanism across the two sources.

cases.text: The model guarantees exact star-arm counts in every natural lake.

evidence.quote: The number of star arms emerges from a stability analysis of this competition

cases.rationale: A stability analysis does not establish an exact universal guarantee. The claim also fails to identify a stated limitation.
